Rashi on Nedarim 6a:1:1.hebrew: דאין אדם מגרש את אשת חבירו - דאי כתב "הרי את מותרת לכל אדם", משמע דלאשתו קאמר, דאשת איניש דעלמא אינו מגרש; ומוכחא מילתא, ושפיר מגרש:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:1:1.english: For a man does not divorce the wife of his fellow - For if he wrote, “You are hereby permitted to any man,” it indicates that he was referring to his wife, as he does not divorce another person’s wife; and the matter is [thus] evident, and he divorces [her] validly.

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:1:2.hebrew: אבל בעלמא - דאי אפשר למימר הכי, בעינן ידים מוכיחות:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:1:2.english: However, in general - Where it is impossible to say so, we require conclusive intimations.

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:2:1.hebrew: אבל לא קאמר עלי לא - דהרי הוא לא משמע כלום, דבעינן ידים מוכיחות:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:2:1.english: However, if he did not say “upon me,” no - For the phrase “it is hereby” does not imply anything, as we require unambiguous intimations.

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:3:1.hebrew: אמר לך אביי - לעולם לא בעינן ידים מוכיחות, והכא היינו טעמא דאי לא אמר בלשון קרבן לא מיתסר: דדלמא ״הרי הוא הפקר״ קאמר, דמוכיחות הוא להפקר או לצדקה:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:3:1.english: Abaye could say to you - Actually, we do not require unambiguous intimations, and here, this is the reason that if he did not speak in the language of an offering it is not forbidden: because perhaps he was saying, “It is hereby ownerless,” for it is an unambiguous intimation for ownerless property or for charity.

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:3:2.hebrew: והא מפני שהוא יד לקרבן קאמר - דאסור כקרבן, ולא מצית אמרת לצדקה או להפקר הוה משמע:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:3:2.english: And does [the baraita] not say: “Because it is an intimation of an offering”? - That it is forbidden like an offering, and you cannot say that it implied [dedication] for charity or for ownerless property.

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:4:1.hebrew: אבל אמר הרי הוא - ולא אמר עלי — שניהם אסורין. דכיון דלא אמר עלי אלא הוא, משמע דחבירו נמי אסור, דה"ק: הרי הוא כהקדש — מה הקדש אסור, אף אותו דבר נמי אסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:4:1.english: However, [if] he said: "It is hereby" - and he did not say "upon me," both of them are forbidden. For since he did not say "upon me," but rather [only] "it," it implies that his fellow is also forbidden, for this is what he is saying: "It is hereby like consecrated property; just as consecrated property is forbidden, so too that item is forbidden."

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:5:1.hebrew: אע"ג דהוא מחויב חטאת ואשם לאו כלום הוא - דלא אמר "עלי", אלמא בעינן ידים מוכיחות:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:5:1.english: Even though he is liable for a sin-offering and a guilt-offering, it is nothing - It is because he did not say “upon me,” which proves that we require unambiguous intimations.

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:5:2.english: If he is liable - To bring a sin-offering or a guilt-offering.

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:5:3.hebrew: דבריו קיימין - הוא דאמר ״חטאתי״. אבל לא היה מחויב חטאת — אינו כלום, הואיל ולא אמר ״עלי״; שאם אמר ״הרי זו עלי חטאת״, אע"ג דלא היה מחויב, הואיל ואמר ״עלי״ — דבריו קיימין:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:5:3.english: His statement takes effect - [This is because] he said: “[This is] my sin-offering”; but [if] he was not obligated to bring a sin-offering, [his statement] is nothing, since he did not say: “[This is] upon me.” For if he said: “This is hereby upon me as a sin-offering,” even though he was not obligated, since he said “upon me,” his statement takes effect.

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:6:1.english: Whose opinion is this - This baraita that said: He did not say anything.

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:6:2.hebrew: רבי יהודה היא - דאמר בעינן ידים מוכיחות, ואנא דאמרי — כרבנן, דאמרי לא בעינן ידים מוכיחות:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:6:2.english: It is Rabbi Yehuda - Who said [that] we require conclusive intimations; and [as for] that which I say, [it is] in accordance with the Rabbis, who say [that] we do not require conclusive intimations.

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:6:3.hebrew: והא אמר אביי אנא דאמרי אפי' לר' יהודה - דלא בעי ידים מוכיחות אלא גבי גט, אבל בעלמא לא. והיכי קאמר הכא ר' יהודה היא:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:6:3.english: “And didn’t Abaye say: ‘I say even according to Rabbi Yehuda’”? - That Rabbi Yehuda does not require conclusive intimations except with regard to a bill of divorce, but in general, he does not; and how does Abaye say here: “It is Rabbi Yehuda”?

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:7:1.hebrew: אלא [לימא] רבא דאמר כר' יהודה - דכיון דאביי לא מתרץ טעמא אליבא דר' יהודה, לימא נמי דרבא לא מתרץ טעמא אליבא דרבנן כדמתרץ לעיל, וכר"י קאמר, דיחידאה היא:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:7:1.english: Rather, shall we say, Rava stated in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - For since Abaye does not explain the reason according to Rabbi Yehuda, shall we say also that Rava does not explain the reason according to the Rabbis as he explained above, and stated his view in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, which is an individual opinion:

Rashi on Nedarim 6a:8:1.hebrew: לא לעולם רבא אפילו לרבנן - כדקאמרינן: ע"כ לא קאמרי רבנן כו', דודאי רבנן סבירא להו בעלמא דידים שאין מוכיחות לא הוויין ידים, כרבא:
Rashi on Nedarim 6a:8:1.english: No, actually, Rava [holds] even according to the Rabbis - As we say: "The Rabbis only say, etc.," for the Rabbis certainly hold in general that intimations that are not obvious are not [valid] intimations, in accordance with Rava.

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:2:1.hebrew: הרי הוא עלי הרי זה עלי אסור - פי': ככר מונח לפניו, אמר "הרי עלי" — אסור, מפני שהוא יד לקרבן, ואסר עליו הככר כקרבן, שכך מתנדב אדם ואומר: "הרי עלי". טעמא דאמר "הרי עלי" — אסור, אבל לא אמר "עלי" — לא; וקשה לאביי:
Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:2:1.english: "It is hereby upon me," "this is hereby upon me," it is forbidden - Explanation: [Where] a loaf was lying before him, [and] he said: "It is hereby upon me" — it is forbidden, because it is an intimation of an offering, and he has forbidden the loaf upon himself like an offering, for this is how a person pledges [a voluntary offering], saying: "It is hereby upon me." The reason it is forbidden is that he said "It is hereby upon me," but if he did not say "upon me," no [it is not forbidden]; and this is difficult for Abaye.

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:3:1.hebrew: אמר לך - כלומר: לכך אי לא אמר "עלי" לא הוי בכלל, ד"הרי הוא הפקר" קאמר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:3:1.english: [Abaye] could have said to you - That is to say: For this reason, if he did not say "upon me," it is not included [in the prohibition], for he was saying: "It is hereby ownerless."

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:3:2.hebrew: והא מפני שהוא יד לקרבן קתני - דמשמע: ד״עלי״ הוי יד מעליא — אסור, אבל אי לא אמר ״עלי״ — יד מיהא הוי; וקשה לאביי, דאמר כו׳:
Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:3:2.english: “But it teaches: Because it is an intimation of an offering” - For it implies that with “upon me” it is a proper intimation and therefore forbidden, but if he did not say “upon me,” it is an intimation nonetheless; and this is difficult for Abaye, who said, etc.:

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:3:3.hebrew: והא מפני שהוא יד לקרבן - כלומר: אינו אלא יד בעלמא, ואינו עיקר הקדש, ואינו אסור אלא לזה ולא לכ"ע:
Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:3:3.english: "And [doesn't the baraita teach]: 'Because it is an intimation of an offering'?" - That is to say: It is merely an intimation [of an offering] and is not actual consecration, and [therefore] it is forbidden only to this [person] and not to everyone.

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:4:1.hebrew: אלא אימא טעמא דאמר עלי הוא דאסור וחבירו מותר - דאי אמר "הרי הוא", אסור לכ"ע; ולאו דווקא שניהם אסורין, כל אחד לדידיה לחודיה, ד"הרי הוא" עיקר הקדש קאמר:
Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:4:1.english: "Rather, say: The reason is that he said 'Upon me', he is forbidden and his fellow is permitted" - For if he said "It is hereby," it is forbidden to everyone; and it is not specifically that only both of them are forbidden, each one for himself alone, for by saying "It is hereby," he is stating the primary formula of consecration.

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:5:1.hebrew: הרי זו חטאת הרי זו אשם - בהמת חולין עוברת לפניו, אמר "הרי זו חטאת" — לא אמר כלום, משום דאין חטאת באה נדבה. ולכך כי אמר "חטאת" ולא אמר "חטאתי", לא אמר ולא כלום, דמשמע שמתנדב חטאת, הלכך חולין הוי. ואף על גב דאמרינן לקמן: ככר לפניו ואמר "הרי זה קרבן" — אסור, יש לומר: דהתם משום דיודע דאי אפשר לככר היותו קרבן, ונתכוין לומר "כקרבן"; אבל הכא, הוא סבור שיכול להתפיס חטאת בנדבה, ולא נתכוין לאסור בהמה כחטאת אלא נדבה, הלכך לא אמר כלום:
Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:5:1.english: "This is hereby a sin-offering, this is hereby a guilt-offering" - [If] an unconsecrated animal was passing before him, [and] he said, "This is hereby a sin-offering," he has said nothing, because a sin-offering cannot be brought as a voluntary offering. And therefore, when he said "a sin-offering" and did not say "my sin-offering," he has said nothing at all, for this implies that he is donating a voluntary sin-offering; therefore, it remains unconsecrated. And even though we say later: [If] a loaf was before him and he said, "This is hereby an offering," it is forbidden [to him] — one can say that there, [it is] because he knows that it is impossible for a loaf to become an [altar] offering, and he intended to say "[it is forbidden to me] like an offering"; but here, he thought that one can dedicate a sin-offering as a voluntary offering, and he did not intend to forbid the animal [to himself] like a sin-offering, but rather [to dedicate it as] a voluntary offering; therefore, he has said nothing.

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:5:2.hebrew: הרי זו חטאתי - אם מחויב חטאת דבריו קיימין. ופריך מרישא, דקאמר "לא אמר כלום", דידים שאין מוכיחות לא הויין ידים; דאי הויין ידים, כי אמר ה"ז לחטאת, היה לנו לאסור כאילו אמר "חטאתי":
Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:5:2.english: "This is hereby my sin-offering" - [The baraita teaches that] if he was liable for a sin-offering, his statement takes effect. And [the Gemara] objects from the opening clause, which states [that] "he has said nothing," [demonstrating] that ambiguous intimations are not [valid] intimations; for if they were [valid] intimations, when he said "This is hereby for a sin-offering," we should have forbidden [the animal], just as if he had said "my sin-offering."

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:6:1.english: In accordance with whose opinion is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda - For he says that ambiguous intimations are not valid intimations.

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:7:1.hebrew: לימא רבא דאמר כרבי יהודה - כי היכי דאביי כרבנן, ה"נ רבא כרבי יהודה ולא כרבנן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:7:1.english: Shall we say that Rava said in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda - Just as Abaye [holds] in accordance with the Rabbis, so too Rava [holds] in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, and not in accordance with the Rabbis.

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:7:2.hebrew: לימא רבא דאמר כר' יהודה - דס"ד, דכי היכי דהדר ביה אביי — ה"נ הדר ביה רבא:
Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:7:2.english: "Shall we say that Rava said in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda?" - For it might enter one's mind that just as Abaye retracted, so too Rava retracted.

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:8:1.hebrew: אמר לך רבא ה"נ אנא דאמרי אפי' לרבנן - כדאמר לעיל, ופליגי רבא ואביי אליבא דרבנן:
Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:8:1.english: Rava could say to you: Here too, I say even according to the Rabbis - As Rava said above, and Rava and Abaye disagree according to the opinion of the Rabbis.

Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:8:2.hebrew: עד כאן לא קאמרי רבנן התם אלא משום דאין אדם מגרש אשת חבירו - כאן משמע דמוכיחות הוי ממינאי, ובגיטין משמע דהוה להוכיח שמגרשה בלא גט; ותרוייהו תננהי. וצ"ע בתוס' ממילתיה דידים שאין מוכיחות:
Tosafot on Nedarim 6a:8:2.english: The Rabbis only say this there because a man does not divorce the wife of his fellow - Here it implies that the issue of conclusive intimations was with regard to the phrase “from me”; and in Gittin it implies that it was necessary to prove that he is divorcing her with this bill of divorce, and not without a bill of divorce; and both of them are taught in the Mishnah. And this requires further study in Tosafot from the discussion of intimations that are not conclusive.
